module: Orbital chase camera, main "external" mode of a vehicle. Orbits around the target point (the vehicle's ref node + offset, or a point imposed by setRef) at a distance camDist; mouse/keyboard rotation (pitch limited to ±85 degrees), zoom (distance between camMinDist and camMaxDist), smoothing, relaxation behind the vehicle, speed-dependent dynamic FOV (dolly zoom effect that keeps the apparent size of the vehicle's rear), dynamic height offset and dynamic pitch above 10 m/s. Uses the collision filter to avoid passing through scenery. Also used by other extensions (couplerCameraModifier). Returns a constructor.
usage:
-- via core_camera, for example to adjust a vehicle's orbit camera:
core_camera.setDistance({vehId = id, camName = 'orbit'}, 8)
core_camera.setDefaultDistance({vehId = id, camName = 'orbit'}, 8)
notes: jbeam configuration fields: distance (5 by default), distanceMin (3), defaultRotation (vec3 degrees, default (0, -17, 0)), offset, mode ('ref' by default), fov (65), skipFovModifier, refNodes. camMaxDist = 10 * distanceMin (or 50 if distanceMin is nil, inferred from code: (distanceMin or 5) * 10).

Settings read: cameraOrbitFovModifier, cameraOrbitRelaxation (3), cameraOrbitMaxDynamicFov (35), cameraOrbitMaxDrivingPitch, cameraOrbitMaxDynamicOffset, cameraOrbitSmoothing, multiseat (in multiseat the dynamic pitch is disabled).
Dynamic FOV: fov = fov + fovModifier + maxDynamicFov * min(1, speed/130). Dynamic height: up to 1.4 * maxDynamicOffset at around 70 m/s.

The extracted page says calculateDynamicPitchLimit(targetPos) but the code takes (data, targetPos); setTargetMode(targetMode, camBase) and setRef(center, left, back) also have more parameters than listed.

Yaw smoothing is limited to the speed maxRot (4.5 rad... value 4.5 per second in automatic input, 1000 if the user turns the camera); onSettingsChanged calls core_camera.clearInputs() (code comment: "is this really necessary?").

C.desc: Orbit mode. Fields: camRot (vec3 degrees: x yaw, y pitch), camDist, camMinDist, camMaxDist, defaultDistance, defaultRotation, fov, offset, orbitOffset, mode, target, lockCamera, collision (instance of the collision filter), smoothingEnabled.

init.desc: Creates the state, the collision filter, then calls onVehicleCameraConfigChanged, onSettingsChanged and reset.

calculateDynamicPitchLimit.desc: Computes (once, cached in dynamicPitchLimit) the maximum downward pitch that keeps the bottom of the vehicle's rear in the field of view.

onVehicleCameraConfigChanged.desc: Hook: reloads distances, default rotation, mode, FOV and resets the dynamic pitch.

onSettingsChanged.desc: Hook: re-reads the cameraOrbit* settings and forwards to the collision filter.

onVehicleSwitched.desc: Hook: forwards to the collision filter.

reset.desc: Reschedules the camera recentering (3 frames) and resets the collision filter; no effect if a recentering is already in progress.

rot.desc: x yaw, y pitch in degrees

serialize.desc: State for video stream views (core_camera get/setContextCameraState): rotation, distance, FOV.

deserialize.desc: Restores the state from serialize and keeps the restored rotation.

listParams.desc: Settings exposed to the camera control UI: dist, smooth, fov.

setOffset.desc: Sets orbitOffset, a world offset added to the camera position.

setRefNodes.desc: Sets the vehicle's reference nodes and the rear node for the dynamic FOV.

dynamicFovRearNodeID.desc: rear node whose on-screen size stays constant during the dynamic FOV effect

setRef.desc: Imposes the target point and the frame in world coordinates (center nil = back to following the vehicle's nodes; a change triggers reset).

setTargetMode.desc: Chooses the target mode ('ref' by default) and the camera offset base.

camBase.desc: base offset in the vehicle frame, nil = computed from offset

setDefaultDistance.desc: Sets the default distance (used when recentering).

setDefaultRotation.desc: Sets the default rotation when recentering.

rot.desc: x yaw, y pitch in degrees

update.desc: Computes the orbit pose and writes data.res (pos, rot, fov, targetPos, collisionCompatible = true), then applies the collision filter.

returns.desc: false if the reference nodes are degenerate, otherwise true
